changes.balance: The premium came out on politics while the balance printed tight: a fifth straight crude draw, distillate at its lowest since May 2003, runs at 94.5 percent, and Midwest utilisation up 4.8 points to 92.9 percent. The congressional constraint behind the repricing binds only from Jan 3, and the desks still price renewed strikes at 60 percent, so the level now carries both a deal path and an escalation branch at once.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled at $94.62 on Wednesday, down $8.98 or 8.7 percent, its lowest close since Aug 31, and WTI Dec26 settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3 percent, its biggest one-day drop since May (Reuters). Brent reached $104.87 in the morning, was $101.30 just after the inventory report, then fell to a $93.22 intraday low after the vice president posted that the war was the reason Republicans lost and the Senate Democratic leader pledged to end the war through the power of the purse. Trend-following funds cut their Brent long share to about 55 percent from 73 percent at the start of the session (Kpler Bridgeton via Bloomberg). Overnight Brent was $94.96, up 0.36 percent, and WTI $87.85, down 0.31 percent, at 0825 GMT in choppy trade. The official report for the week ending Oct 30 drew crude by 0.865 million barrels, drew distillate by 3.565 million to its lowest since May 2003, and lifted PADD 2 utilisation 4.8 points to 92.9 percent. December WCS is -$31.08 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 4) on 120 lots, and December Houston is -$21.23 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 4) on 165 lots, putting the export spread at +$9.86. The validated diesel crack is $88.73 on the Nov 5 print.
changes.conditional: A second settle near $94 with time spreads stabilising grades Wednesday as a premium level reset; a recovery through $100 on an escalation headline grades it as a stop-run inside an unchanged premium structure. A published acceptance in the mediator process would start the reopening sequence the price is now discounting.
changes.delta: Wednesday settles: Brent Jan27 $94.62, down $8.98 or 8.7 percent; WTI Dec26 $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3 percent (Reuters). Overnight Brent $94.96 and WTI $87.85 at 0825 GMT. EIA week ending Oct 30: crude -0.865 million barrels, distillate -3.565 million to 99.3 million, utilisation 94.5 percent, PADD 2 utilisation 92.9 percent. December WCS -$31.08 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 4) on 120 lots. December Houston -$21.23 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 4) on 165 lots, spread +$9.86. Diesel crack $88.73 on the validated history.
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 4-5, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 4, 2026; EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, released Nov 4, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 4, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 5, 2026
changes.title: Brent fell $8.98 to its lowest close since Aug 31 as the market repriced the war premium, and the inventory report printed a fifth straight draw with Midwest utilisation up 4.8 points

changes.balance: The fall maintenance season is confirmed closed at its three largest open items, which removes the supply and demand outage legs from the wide front's support. What holds December wide is now only apportionment and freight, against record supply and a repaired Midwest refinery gate.
changes.body: Cenovus Energy released third quarter results on Nov 4: net earnings of $3,360 million, adjusted funds flow of $5,023 million, upstream production a record 1,023.5 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day and Oil Sands production a record 833.0, with downstream throughput of 437.2 kb/d at 92 percent. The release states the Lima refinery turnaround was completed in October; the 40 to 50 kb/d fourth quarter US refining impact it still carries is the quarterly average drag of the October outage portion. Suncor Energy's Nov 4 webcast declared the 37-day Edmonton refinery turnaround complete, with major maintenance for the year completed; the guided Base Plant fourth quarter item was not addressed and stays open. Canadian Natural Resources reports this morning with the Horizon return still unconfirmed.
changes.conditional: A Horizon return confirmation from Canadian Natural closes the last major fall item; silence keeps it unverified into the December nominations window. A Base Plant statement from Suncor, in either direction, closes the remaining guided item.
changes.delta: Cenovus Q3 (Nov 4): net earnings $3,360 million, adjusted funds flow $5,023 million, upstream a record 1,023.5 MBOE/d, Oil Sands a record 833.0 MBOE/d, downstream 437.2 kb/d at 92 percent; Lima turnaround completed in October. Suncor webcast (Nov 4): Edmonton 37-day turnaround declared complete, major maintenance for the year completed; Base Plant fourth quarter item not addressed.
changes.source: Cenovus Energy third quarter 2026 results, Nov 4, 2026; Suncor Energy third quarter webcast, Nov 4, 2026
changes.title: Lima and Edmonton turnarounds are confirmed complete, and record Cenovus volumes close the fall maintenance season's main items

changes.balance: The reserve programme is now fully awarded and fully scheduled: crude exchanges complete at 172 million barrels with returns from early next year, and the heating oil exchange closes with deliveries due Nov 6. The remaining reserve content is return timing, not new supply decisions.
changes.body: Checked directly on Nov 5, the Energy Department's newest reserve item is the Northeast heating oil reserve award: a release published Nov 3 and updated Nov 4 awards 300,000 barrels of ultra-low-sulfur diesel out of 315,000 offered, for Boston and New Haven, with deliveries due by Nov 6, 2026. Reuters (Nov 4) names the awardees as Global Companies, Sprague Operating Resources, Trafigura Trading and Vitol. No new crude solicitation or award has posted since the Oct 29 award completing the 172 million barrel commitment, and no posting dated Nov 5 had appeared at run time.
changes.conditional: Any change to the posted award sheets, or a delivery schedule from the Department, updates the return timing. A new solicitation would reopen the programme.
changes.delta: Correction to the Nov 4 check: the heating oil reserve award posted Nov 3 (300,000 barrels, Boston and New Haven, deliveries due Nov 6, not Nov 13 as previously carried). No other change: newest crude item remains the Oct 29 award completing the 172 million barrel commitment.
changes.source: US Department of Energy newsroom and SPR pages, checked directly Nov 5, 2026; Reuters, Nov 4, 2026
changes.title: Reserves: the heating oil award posted on Nov 3 with deliveries due Nov 6, closing the last open reserve item

flags.body: Brent settled at $94.62 on Wednesday, down $8.98, after post-election statements pointed toward ending the war and trend-following funds cut their Brent long share from 73 to about 55 percent intraday. Tehran's conditions are unchanged, the mediator feedback window lapsed with no reported outcome, and Wednesday's concrete US action designated a false-flag registry network supplying Iran's shadow fleet. Eurasia Group prices renewed strikes at 60 percent with a $110 to $125 Brent band, a deal at 10 percent and a standoff at 30 percent. The new Congress is seated Jan 3, 2027; until then the administration's foreign policy runs under the existing composition.
flags.title: The war premium repriced on politics: no deal, no accepted terms, and the escalation branch still priced at 60 percent
flags.trigger: A published agreement or acceptance in the mediator process, a confirmed strike or maritime escalation, a second settle confirming or reversing Wednesday's level, or the Jan 3 seating of the new Congress

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call now includes four wide traded December settlements in five sessions (-$31.10 on Oct 28, -$30.69 on Nov 2, -$31.25 on Nov 3 and -$31.08 on Nov 4) and a deferred strip that tightened on 580-lot volume in April through June, pricing the episode's exit. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.body: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003 and 13 percent below the five-year average, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. PADD 2 distillate drew 1.4 million to 22.8 million in the same week. The validated diesel crack is $88.73, off its highs but still a tight-products price, and total commercial petroleum inventories fell 8.2 million barrels on the week. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12.
flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction
